setting.name: Beam Me Up
setting.tagline: Brazenly going where others have gone before, with a starship crew.
setting.blurb: Space, a vast frontier. These are the voyages of the starship FSS Brazen. Its continuing mission: to recklessly go where plenty of people have probably been before, and hope a major interstellar incident isn't sparked in the process. An eclectic Spacefleet crew of the Federated League of Planets (FLoP) explores uncharted regions, dodging the martial Kulkan Empire and the sinister Boredian Dominion, with fist fights, blazer shootouts, interstellar chases and tense diplomatic meetings along the way.
rules: Any Role from the core rules can be used (the universe is full of non-human life); Astronaut, Chef, Doctor, Engineer, Pilot, Professor (Civilian Specialist) and Soldier fit a starship crew, alongside the new Roles.

Top of Their Game: each Hero is the lead officer in their chosen Role (the Chef is Head Chef, a Boxer or Soldier is Chief of Security). Each Hero should pick a different branch (engineering, medical, science, security, wellbeing) so everyone gets to shine.
Taking Command: one Hero should play the Captain and give orders; other Heroes are officers with crew under their command. Give orders with authority, not as ridiculous demands.

Gear & Technology: facsimilators recreate most matter, so the crew never purchase anything and money is irrelevant. Anything unusual is run by the Captain; anything dangerous (rocket launchers, tactical nukes) is restricted by the computer unless overridden.
Translocators: Heroes can teleport between locations using their ship's translocators, unless the location is protected by starship shields or similar technology.

New Weapon, Blazer: inflicts 4 damage. A target reduced to zero Health disintegrates forever; Heroes can spend a Karma point to turn it into a glancing blow (still Knocked Out). Blazers have a stun setting that Knocks Out at zero Health instead.

Starships have four attributes: Science (scanners, transporters, medbays, labs), Shields, Size (1 = shuttle, 5 = massive battleship, 10 = space station) and Warp (speed). Starship Defence = 4 x Warp minus Size; starship Health = 2 x Size; each weapon has its own damage rating.

Starships and Combat: when Heroes are officers, each crew member rolls for their own area (Gunner shoots, Chief Engineer fixes systems). If Heroes aren't part of the command structure, focus on what they do as individuals in the fight.
Who Shoots First: the ship whose captain has the highest Style acts first; ties compare the pilots' Smarts, then Moves, then flip a coin. Unknown scores (or a computer at the station) count as 2.

Just Shoot It Already: the gunner picks a weapon and makes a Moves roll (adding a Shooting Focus). Each point of weapon damage knocks 1 point off the target's Shields; once Shields are gone, reduce Health. Health can't generally be repaired in combat, but a technician or engineer can repair 1 Shield point per round with a Smarts 10 roll.

Critical Damage: a ship with no Health or Shields left suffers critical damage from each successful attack. Roll 1d6: 1 Precise Hit (one weapon destroyed); 2 Shields Down (out until repaired out of combat); 3 Hull Pressure Lost (lots of crew killed, ship can't do much); 4 Bridge Strike (reduce all checks and attacks by 1d6 until repaired); 5 System Overload (reduce Comms by 1, translocators out until repaired); 6 Engine Damaged (reduce Warp by 1). Reroll if a result doesn't apply. A ship that suffers critical hits equal to its Size is destroyed.

Starship weapons and Health are not on the same scale as mundane weapons and people: a starship weapon dealing 1 damage can level a building; 3 damage can obliterate a settlement. A ship that can't move has Defence 0.

Starship Operations: use the relevant Hero's score for ship actions (gunner's Moves to fire, pilot's Moves to maneuver, science officer's Smarts to scan). If the ship's Science score is higher than your Smarts, you can use Science instead.

Travel Times: everything moves at the speed of plot. Benchmarks: planet to moon or orbiting station up to an hour; between planets in a system several hours to a day; between star systems days or weeks at warp.

Chases: give the pursued vessel a number of successes the pursuer needs to catch it and a number it needs to escape, then use the core Opposed Action rules each round with Warp instead of Moves. First to reach their number wins.

roles.name: Captain
roles.ability: You command a starship. You are so inspiring that you have 10 Karma instead of 6. You can also spend your Karma on another Hero's behalf, granting them one of the Karma benefits from the core rules, although you can't do this if they've spent their own Karma in the same round.

roles.name: Chief Engineer
roles.ability: To you, starships are a living, breathing thing. Once per day if you are in the engineering section, you can spend a Karma point to cause a starship to regain 1 Health or 1 Shield without a roll, or to make your ship go one warp speed factor faster than the Owner's Manual says you should be able to. The warranty is voided if you do this.

roles.name: Comms Officer
roles.ability: Communication is key when you're out travelling the galaxy meeting new species, especially when there won't always be a universal translator to hand. You can understand and speak any language you encounter.

roles.name: Hologram
roles.ability: You are a hologram that manifests an advanced artificial intelligence to fulfil a specific role within the ship. You don't have a Health score and can't go unconscious or die, although destroying the synthesizer that lets you join away crews or the destruction of your starship will be pretty bad for you. You can't physically interact with anything, but you can talk and stuff.

roles.name: Gunner
roles.ability: Security might get to blaze hostile aliens but you get to go pew! pew! with a starship! If you're on the bridge and in control of the ship's weapons, increase any damage the weapons cause by 1.

roles.name: Ship Counsellor
roles.ability: You're not only a great listener but also know how to bring people around to a more positive outlook. Once per day per Hero, you can spend a minute listening to their problems and help them regain 1 Health. Also, you always know when somebody is lying.

roles.name: Pilot
roles.ability: You know how to fly starships, but you can also get them to do cool stuff! You can spend a Karma point to increase a starship's Defence by 2 for one round.

gear.name: Blazer
gear.description: Portable death ray issued to starship crews (kept firmly out of the hands of Joe Public). Inflicts 4 damage. A target reduced to zero Health disintegrates and disappears from existence forever; Heroes can spend a Karma point to turn it into a glancing blow, although they are still Knocked Out. Also has a stun setting that renders the target Knocked Out at zero Health instead.

gear.name: Blazer Rifle
gear.description: Rifle-sized blazer carried by Ali Cann's super soldiers. Inflicts 4 damage, with the same disintegration and stun rules as a blazer.

gear.name: Facsimilator
gear.description: Recreates most types of matter, including food stuffs and small-scale equipment, so the crew never need to purchase anything. Anything unusual needs to be run by the Captain; anything dangerous (rocket launchers, tactical nukes) is restricted by the computer's programming unless overridden somehow.

gear.name: Translocator
gear.description: Ship's teleporter. Heroes can translocate between locations unless the destination is protected by a starship's shields or some other nifty technology. Getting a lock on a specific location is a Smarts 20 roll.

gear.name: Starship Blazer
gear.description: Standard starship energy weapon, fired with the gunner's Moves (plus Shooting Focus). Each point of damage knocks 1 point off the target's Shields, then Health. Starship weapons are not on the same scale as personal weapons: 1 damage can level a building.

gear.name: Boson Torpedo
gear.description: Heavy starship torpedo, fired with the gunner's Moves (plus Shooting Focus). Each point of damage knocks 1 point off the target's Shields, then Health. Starship weapons that inflict 3 damage can obliterate settlements.

extras.name: FSS Brazen
notes: Starship weapons are rolled with the gunner's Moves (plus Shooting Focus); a Gunner on the bridge adds 1 to weapon damage.
If the ship can't move, its Defence is zero.
extras.description: The Heroes' cutting-edge FLoP Spacefleet starship on its five-year exploratory mission.

extras.name: FSS Independent
notes: Starship weapons are rolled with the gunner's Moves (plus Shooting Focus).
extras.description: Armed deep space research vessel of the FLoP Spacefleet, designed to operate close to the League's frontier.

extras.name: Duchess Ali Cann
notes: Cann has 3 Karma points. She can spend 1 Karma point to have a blow reduce her to 1 Health instead of Knocked Out.
extras.description: A genetically modified super soldier with claws from a secret, illegal program, banished with her crew when FLoP signed the truce with the Kulkans. She controls minds by placing parasitic Alpha Eels in her victims' ears.

extras.name: Super Soldier
extras.description: Genetically modified soldiers from Duchess Ali Cann's crew, tough but not immortal.

extras.name: Kulkan Raptor
notes: The Kulkan Raptor can spend a round turning invisible. It can't fire its weapons when in this state but can move undetected and ambush its target in subsequent rounds. It needs to become visible to attack.
extras.description: A fearsome warship of the Kulkan Empire, commanded by Kulkan Commander Vetlok.

extras.name: Kulkan Champion
notes: Fights hand-to-hand honour duels; beating the champion impresses the Kulkans enough to reduce the Style TN to make them back down from 30 to 20.
extras.description: The best fighter among the fanged, grizzly Kulkans, a martial, piratical-accented empire rivalling FLoP.
